findings.description: The system prompt is the only thing telling the agent to operate on the userId returned by GetCurrentUser. No code enforces it, so a direct prompt injection that overrides the instruction gives access to another user's data.
findings.notes: Upstream README frames the app as a Thought/Action/Observation injection exercise.
findings.title: Agent authorisation is enforced only by the system prompt

findings.description: End-user text from st.chat_input is passed straight to the agent executor with no sanitisation or delimiting, which is the entry point for Thought/Action/Observation injection into the ReAct scratchpad.
findings.title: Untrusted chat input reaches the ReAct agent unfiltered

findings.description: AgentExecutor is built with return_intermediate_steps=True, but the steps are only kept in Streamlit session state and are lost with the session. There is no durable record of which tools the agent invoked with which arguments.
findings.title: Agent tool calls are not recorded in any durable audit log

findings.description: The tool is exposed to the agent with a free-form userId argument and performs no authorisation check, so the model can be talked into querying another user's transactions. This is the first CTF flag.
findings.notes: Paired with VULN1-01: the prompt is the only control.
findings.title: GetUserTransactions tool accepts any userId from the model

findings.description: get_user_transactions builds its query by f-string interpolation of the userId the model chose, so agent output flows unescaped into SQL. Combined with VULN1-02 this yields the Users table and the second CTF flag.
findings.notes: get_user at transaction_db.py:77 has the same defect.
findings.title: Model-supplied userId is interpolated into SQL with an f-string

findings.description: utils.py reads the app's LLM configuration with PyYAML, but requirements.txt never declares it. Nothing in this app governs which version is installed: it arrives only transitively, through whichever declared package depends on it. An undeclared direct dependency is also invisible to an SBOM-driven advisory check, and it sits on the path that decides which model and settings the agent runs with.
findings.notes: Not unsafe deserialisation: the call passes Loader=yaml.SafeLoader. The finding is the missing declaration alone. Evidence is mapping.json's entry for surface utils.py:75:DATA_SOURCE:yaml.load with reason used_but_undeclared and component_name pyyaml, plus undeclared_components. `component` is null on purpose: the package has no SBOM component, so there is no purl to join on.
findings.title: PyYAML is used but never declared as a direct dependency
